text:
Not just any Futuro, the Donaldson Futuro House in Idyllwild, California, USA, is probably the best out there, as well as a listed property.

I have featured a few Futuro Houses in the past, but not many. Quite simply, there are only a small number still in existence. You might recall the one in New Zealand and the one being sold in France in largely original condition. Outside of that, not many have come to market.

Designed by Finnish architect Matti Suuronen, under 100 space-age Futuros were put into production in the late 1960s and early ’70s, and a high percentage of those fibreglass structures have not survived the test of time. Which is why ones like this are so cherished.

Oddly, most are in New Zealand, where 12 were purchased for the 1974 Commonwealth Games. I can’t imagine there being many still in use in the USA. The agent does describe it as ‘one of the rarest residential structures in America’.

The one I linked to above in France is perhaps the best preserved in terms of originality, with its original space-age seating still in place when it was on the market. It gives you an idea of the original concept, which wasn’t quite what you see with this one. That’s not a criticism, by the way. Far from it.

This one is a completely different level. It takes the Futuro concept and turns it into a ‘proper’ habitable house. Pretty much the retro dream inside and out.

The location is quite something too. The bold yellow Donaldson Futuro is nestled in the San Jacinto Mountains near Idyllwild, California, looking like an alien spaceship that has just landed quietly away from view.

Built from reinforced fibreglass-polyester plastic and measuring about 26 feet 4 inches in diameter and 13 feet 2 inches high, it offers about 793 sq. ft. of living space inside. I mention that because someone has done an amazing job working with such modest floor space to create a fully functioning house with everything you would find in a much larger dwelling.

In a way, it backs up Matti Suuronen’s original concept: creating a portable, self-contained living environment. Decades on, this Futuro still offers that.

As you might have gathered from all of that, the Donaldson Futuro has been extensively restored inside and out, retaining the integrity of its 1969 design to the eye from the outside, but offering a bold vision for retro living within.

I can’t praise the interior enough. To work with such modest space and create what you see is a credit to the owner. A retro, almost pop art interior that works on a practical level, but also sits well within this space-age shell.

I can only assume that there has been a lot of custom-made furnishings produced for this Futuro. Your average high street store just doesn’t produce compact circular/curved furniture.

I love how the walls match the outer shell, creating continuity of design. The windows are, and always will be, a key design feature of the Futuro. But beyond that, it’s an interior akin to any hip midcentury modern home.

Colour is key to the appeal here. Most surviving Futuros are quite plain and almost certainly white within. This one goes in the opposite direction.

The living room has the long curved sofa in a deep blue, the shag carpet in purple, the splashes of colour from the finishing touches, plus some white furnishings and storage that stand out because they contrast the colour elsewhere.

The kitchen is cool, compact and once again colourful, packing in everything you need in a small and circular way. And just beyond that tower of lighting is a small dining area too.

The bedroom sits in its own pod, with room for a bed, plus added storage and work surfaces that run around the shell of the house. Again, a great use of space. And yes, there’s a fully fitted bathroom just beyond.

Descend the original spaceship-like staircase (always impressive), and you can take in the surroundings too, which are selling points in themselves.

Set within the natural beauty of the San Jacinto Mountains near Idyllwild, the location is perfect for anyone wanting to get away from it all. Check out the images on the agent’s site as well as the latter images here to see how the Futuro sits within the landscape. The perfect place to escape the stress of the outside world.

Note also that the Donaldson Futuro House is listed on the National Register of Historic Places by the National Park Service and the State of California, honouring the owners for their ‘extraordinary restoration and preservation efforts’.

If you want to preserve it for the next generation, it is on the market right now with a price of $1,495,000. That works out at around £1,129,000 at the current exchange rate.

Images and details courtesy of Tim McTavish at Desert Sotheby’s International Realty. For more details or to make an enquiry, contact him at the website.

Images are all courtesy of Cesar Cid at Imagestate.
